title: st.spinner doesnt animate in recent versions (at least 1.60, and 1.61)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hi,

For the last few versions of streamlit I have noticed that st.spinner doesnt animate for me. It just shows the circle with the black segment at the top for the duration of the spinner.

I've tested on Chrome and Edge on upto date Windows 11.

I see the problem on the documentation example.

https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/status/st.spinner

The time animates, but the circle doesn't.

Appreciate any guidance for how to fix this.

Thanks
Mike


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time

with st.spinner("Wait for it...", show_time=True):
    time.sleep(5)
st.success("Done!")
st.button("Rerun")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Goto https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/status/st.spinner
2. Scroll to Examples section.
3. Observe the spinner, or click Rerun to run it again.

### Expected Behavior

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-16598)

The spinner circle is a CSS-animated border (`StyledSpinnerIcon`) while the elapsed-time text is updated in JS. That matches this report: on 1.60/1.61 the timer still ticks, but the circle stays frozen with the dark segment at the top (the `rotate(0deg)` rest pose). Since 1.58 ([#15163](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/15163)), the BaseWeb spinner was replaced with a custom CSS rotation that also disables animation under `[USER] (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`. That is the most likely cause here: the reporter sees it in both Chrome and Edge on Windows 11, including the docs example, which Chromium maps from **Settings → Accessibility → Visual effects → Animation effects**. Worth confirming that OS setting (and whether a non-`show_time` spinner is also static) before treating this as a general animation regression.

### Related Issues

No duplicate of a non-rotating `st.spinner` icon was found. Closest related issues:

- [#13387](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/13387) — Same docs/`show_time=True` spinner example; a closed visual styling bug (timer alignment), not the rotation itself.
- [#11720](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11720) — Closed bug about the spinner **timer** pausing when the tab is backgrounded, which is the JS clock path rather than the CSS circle animation.
- [#14555](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/14555) — Open spinner visual issue (cache spinner overlapping a progress bar); same component, different symptom.

[USER] can you check your accessibility settings as suggested in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16598#issuecomment-5369623258? You can also check this by running the following in the browser dev console:

```
window.matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches
```

Hi [USER], Thanks for following up, I can confirm that reactivating the Animation Effects toggle restores the functionality. However, reading the AI synopsis of the Animation Effects suggests it is intended for window reveal/movement animations, menus etc. not active progress updates (see below). I have Windows Animation Effects turned off as I like to have windows mini/maximise immediately etc. Maybe this could be reverted? Many thanks Mike
